title: Read an INI file
description:
Write `parseIni(text)`, which reads INI-style data into a map from `"section.key"` to value, and reports errors with line numbers.

Rules, line by line (lines are separated by `\n`; ignore a `\r` at the end of a line):

- Blank lines and lines whose first non-space character is `;` or `#` are ignored.
- `[name]` starts a section. Keys before any section belong to the section `""`, stored as `".key"`.
- `key = value` stores a value. Spaces around the key and the value are trimmed. The value may contain `=`.
- Anything else is an error: record `"line N: ..."` (N counted from 1, the message after the colon is up to you) and carry on.
- A key repeated in the same section keeps the **last** value.

```
; enemies
[goblin]
health = 30
name = Goblin = small

->  "goblin.health" = "30", "goblin.name" = "Goblin = small"
```
hints: Read line by line with `std::getline` on an `std::istringstream`, counting lines. Trim each line, then decide: ignore, section, key-value, or error.
For key-value lines, split at the **first** `=`: the key is before it, the value (which may contain more `=`) after it. Trim both.
